To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Ribonuclease‐A is inactivated when UV‐A light irradiated in the presence of a photosensitizer.
ribonuclease A was modified by UV irradiation in the presence of the photosensitizing drug psoralen.

(i) ribonuclease A inactivation by UV‐A irradiation in the presence of sporalen is due to the binding of the drug to protein amino acid residues, which is accompanied by the oxidation of some of them, and (ii) this binding is not selective for a few amino acid residues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the photomodified ribonuclease in the hope of gaining some understanding of the mechanism of action of the enzyme and of the photomutagenic effect.
the modification of ribonuclesase by near‐UV irradiation in the presence of the photoreactive drug.
the study of the modification of proteins and nucleic acids by UV‐A irradiation, in the presence of a photosensitizer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ribonuclease‐A is a protein with a very low photoreactivity in the near‐UV region of the spectrum in the presence of a singlet oxygen sensitizer.

the modification of ribonuclese A by UV‐A irradiation in the presence of 5‐methylpsoralen occurs with low selectivity, and that the amino acid residues most affected are those known to be involved with the catalytic activity.
the photomodied ribonuclease A presents a very complex modification, which is not limited to a few amino acid residues, but involves a wide range of the peptide chain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ribonuclease‐psoralen complex is a very unstable one. which undergoes a rapid degradation in the absence of oxygen, but is very stable in its oxidized form.
psoralen is able to bind to ribonuclease in the presence of UV‐A light and that this binding occurs at several points on the polypeptide chain.
psoralen is a very poor photomodifying agent, since it reacts indiscriminately with all the amino acids in the ribonuclease A molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
psoralen photomodification of proteins is a rather unspecific process and that, as a consequence, the interpretation of the biological consequences of the reaction is not straightforward.
ribonuclease A can be inactivated by UV‐A in the presence of the psoralen, but with a low selectivity.

the photomodiﬁcation of ribonuclese A by UV‐A radiation is not a very selective process and the amino acid residues which are most affected are not the same as those affected by chemical modification.
